court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Additional Sessions Judge, Majalgaon in Sessions Case No.32 of 2012
case_name: Ashok Dadarao Sable vs The State Of Maharashtra

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ashok s/o Dadarao Sable, husband and father of three sons

facts_of_case: Accused Ashok married Anita ten years ago, begot three sons. He started doubting her character and ill-treated her. She left the house and started residing with her parents. Accused filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The benefit of doubt ought to be given to the Appellant.
legal_principles.held: In support of his submission that the benefit of doubt ought to be given to the Appellant, he placed reliance on the Judgment in the case of Sanjay vs. State of Maharashtra, (2007) 9 S.C.C. 148.
cited_cases: Sanjay vs. State of Maharashtra, (2007) 9 S.C.C. 148

legal_principles.principle: Dying declarations are consistent, reliable and there is no variance at all as regards the role attributed to the Appellant.
legal_principles.held: All the dying declarations are consistent, reliable and there is no variance at all as regards the role attributed to the Appellant.
cited_cases: Shaikh Juned Shaikh Moti Mansuri and another vs. State of Maharashtra and another, 2014(2) Mh.L.J. (Cri.) 131

outcome.final_order: Appellant convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to suffer life imprisonment with fine, and also convicted under Section 498-A IPC and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine. Both sentences were directed to run concurrently.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
